## Purpose and Runtime
Apache Answer is a self-hosted Q&A, help-center, and knowledge-management platform. It ships as a Go backend plus React frontend, typically packaged in a Docker image and deployed with persistent `/data` storage. Primary runtime/build entry points are `cmd/main.go`, `cmd/command.go`, and `cmd/wire_gen.go`; container startup is defined by `Dockerfile` and `script/entrypoint.sh`.

## Application Composition and Startup
The Go executable uses Cobra commands and Google Wire-generated dependency injection. Startup assembles configuration, repositories, services, HTTP server, scheduled work, and routes through provider modules rather than a single monolith initializer. Installation is a first-class server mode that can bootstrap configuration from environment values.
- `cmd/main.go`
- `cmd/wire.go`
- `internal/install/install_server.go`

## HTTP, UI, and API Boundary
The backend hosts API, static/UI, Swagger, template-rendered, plugin, and MCP endpoints. Requests pass through shared middleware for recovery, authentication, API keys, language, rate limiting, and specialized plugin/MCP access controls before controllers invoke services. The React SPA is the principal interactive client; server HTML templates support rendered/public pages and SEO-oriented views.
- `internal/base/server/http.go`
- `internal/router/config.go`
- `internal/router/mcp_router.go`
- `ui/src/router/routes.ts`
- `ui/static.go`

## Core Domain and Layering
Domain operations follow a controller → service → repository → entity pattern. Controllers expose public/admin workflows; services enforce content, permissions, revisions, reviews, voting, tags, collections, badges, notifications, and user/account policies; repositories persist and query entities. API schemas form the request/response boundary, distinct from persistence entities.
- `internal/controller/question_controller.go`
- `internal/service/content/question_service.go`
- `internal/repo/question/question_repo.go`
- `internal/entity/question_entity.go`
- `internal/schema/question_schema.go`

## Persistence, Installation, and Configuration
Persistent state includes users/authentication, questions/answers/comments, tags, revisions, reviews, notifications, plugin configuration/KV data, API keys, and site configuration. Versioned migrations initialize and evolve the schema; installation can be driven interactively or from environment settings. Configuration defaults and runtime loading are centralized outside individual features.
- `configs/config.yaml`
- `configs/config.go`
- `internal/migrations/migrations.go`
- `internal/migrations/init_data.go`
- `internal/base/conf/conf.go`

## Asynchronous and Derived Work
In-process queue abstractions and cron support decouple side effects from request handling: activity tracking, event processing, notification/email delivery, search indexing, and vector/embedding synchronization. This is a material boundary for changes that create content or user events: synchronous domain writes can trigger downstream queue/event work.
- `internal/base/queue/queue.go`
- `internal/base/cron/cron.go`
- `internal/service/eventqueue/event_queue.go`
- `internal/service/notification/notification_service.go`
- `internal/service/vector_sync/vector_sync.go`

## Extensibility and External Integrations
A typed plugin contract exposes replaceable or additive capabilities including authentication/user center, CAPTCHA, CDN/storage/upload, search/vector search, parsers/rendering, connectors/importers, review, filtering, notifications, and plugin KV storage. AI conversations, embeddings, and MCP routes provide AI-agent-facing integration points. Implementations can therefore cross external boundaries without embedding provider-specific logic into core content services.
- `plugin/plugin.go`
- `plugin/search.go`
- `plugin/vector_search.go`
- `internal/service/ai_conversation/ai_conversation_service.go`
- `internal/controller/mcp_controller.go`

## Deployment and Frontend Delivery
The frontend is a React/TypeScript application with route-level public, user, review, install, and administration surfaces; its service clients call backend APIs. Docker Compose and Helm provide local and Kubernetes deployment paths, with deployment, service, ingress, PVC, and autoscaling manifests.
- `ui/src/index.tsx`
- `ui/src/services/index.ts`
- `docker-compose.yaml`
- `charts/templates/deployment.yaml`
- `charts/templates/pvc.yaml`
